title: Preventing Sourdough Focaccia from Sticking to Pan
meta_description: Learn how to keep sourdough focaccia from sticking with simple tricks, proper pan prep, and the best non‑stick silicone baking mats for flawless results.
html:
When you pull a golden, airy sourdough focaccia out of the oven, the last thing you want is a stuck bottom that tears the crust. The secret lies in proper pan preparation and the right surface—enter the sourdough focaccia non stick mat. Using a silicone baking mat eliminates the need for parchment, reduces cleanup, and ensures a clean release every time.

Choose the Right Pan and Size

Focaccia thrives in a pan that can accommodate generous expansion. A heavy‑bottomed, rimmed sheet pan (10×15 inches) offers even heat distribution and prevents hot spots that can cause sticking. If you’re working with a smaller loaf, a 9‑inch round pan works, but be aware that the dough will spread less, increasing the chance of a dry edge.

Pre‑Season the Pan or Use a Silicone Baking Mat

There are two reliable ways to create a non‑stick surface:

  1. Traditional method: Lightly coat the pan with a thin layer of high‑quality olive oil, then sprinkle a handful of coarse sea salt. The oil forms a barrier, while the salt adds flavor and texture.
  2. Modern method: Lay a silicone baking mat directly on the pan. These mats are non‑stick, reusable, and can replace parchment entirely. The mat’s heat‑resistant surface allows the focaccia to brown beautifully without the dough clinging to the metal.

When you want a truly sourdough focaccia non stick mat experience, the silicone option wins for consistency and easy cleanup. Just press the mat onto the pan, and you’re ready to go.

Mind the Dough Hydration and Handling

High‑hydration focaccias (70‑80% water) are deliciously airy but also prone to sticking if over‑handled. After the first rise, gently turn the dough onto a well‑floured surface, stretch it to fit the pan, and avoid excessive flour that can create a dry crust. Let the dough rest on the mat or oiled pan for the second rise—this short rest (30‑45 minutes) lets the gluten relax, making the dough easier to lift.

Temperature and Baking Tips

Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C) and bake the focaccia on the middle rack. A hot oven creates steam, which keeps the interior moist while the bottom crisps. If you’re using a silicone baking mat, you’ll notice the bottom browns evenly because the mat conducts heat without the dough adhering to the metal.

Halfway through baking, rotate the pan for uniform color. For an extra‑crisp bottom, switch the oven to convection for the last five minutes—just keep an eye on the edges to prevent burning.

Cooling and Removing Without Damage

After the focaccia reaches a deep golden hue and sounds hollow when tapped, remove it from the oven and let it rest for five minutes. This short cooling period allows the crust to set, reducing the risk of tearing when you lift it.

If you used a silicone baking mat, simply slide a thin metal spatula under the dough, lift, and set it on a cooling rack. The mat releases the focaccia cleanly, leaving no burnt spots on the pan. If you opted for oil and salt, use a spatula to loosen the edges before gently flipping the pan upside down.

Cleaning Up the Right Way

Cleaning the pan is where the silicone baking mat really shines. After the focaccia cools, let the mat cool as well, then rinse it with warm, soapy water. No scrubbing pads are needed—any residue wipes away effortlessly. For the pan itself, a quick wipe with a paper towel or a soft cloth is enough, since the oil layer has protected the surface.

FAQ

Can I use a silicone baking mat for any type of bread?

Yes. Silicone mats are safe up to 480°F (250°C) and work well for most yeasted breads, including ciabatta, baguettes, and pizza.

Do I need to grease the silicone mat before baking?

No. The mat’s non‑stick surface eliminates the need for additional oil or parchment, though a light brush of olive oil can add flavor if desired.

How do I keep my silicone mat from absorbing odors?

After each use, wash the mat with mild dish soap and rinse thoroughly. For persistent smells, a soak in a mixture of water and baking soda works well.
